cards.text: One of the Pharisees invites Jesus over to eat, so Jesus goes in and reclines at the table. Dinner at a Pharisee's house, friend. I bet it's the kind of place where you're scared to set your cookie down ANYWHERE.
Then a woman from that town finds out Jesus is dining there. The text calls her a sinful woman, and she comes to that house carrying something.

cards.question: What does the sinful woman bring with her to the Pharisee's house?

cards.text: She stands behind Jesus, right at His feet, and she's weeping. Her tears start falling on His feet.

cards.question: The woman wipes Jesus' feet with her own hair.
The woman kisses Jesus' feet. Then what does she do with her perfume?

answers.text: She anoints His feet with it
She pours it over His head
She hands it to the Pharisee

cards.text: The Pharisee who invited Jesus sees all of this and says something to himself. Not out loud, just that little inside voice we ALL have.

cards.question: The Pharisee tells himself that if Jesus were a prophet, He would know what kind of woman is touching Him.

cards.text: He only said it to himself, and Jesus ANSWERS him anyway. That's like me grumbling about my oven timer in my head and the timer going, "I heard that."

cards.question: Jesus says to the Pharisee, "___, I have something to tell you."
Simon, the Pharisee who invited Jesus, hears that Jesus has something to tell him. What does Simon say?

cards.text: So Jesus tells Simon a story. Two men owe money to the same moneylender.

cards.question: One man owes the moneylender five hundred denarii. The other owes ___ denarii.

cards.text: Neither man can pay him back. You know the feeling: open the bill, close the bill, open it AGAIN like the number got smaller while you weren't looking.

cards.question: The moneylender forgives only the man who owed fifty denarii.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns the story into a question for Simon. Story time just became quiz time, friend.

cards.question: Jesus asks Simon which of the two men will love the moneylender more. What does Simon say?

answers.text: The one who was forgiven more
The one who was forgiven less
Both of them about the same

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon that he has judged correctly.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns toward the woman, but He's still talking to Simon: "Do you see this woman?" And He walks Simon back through the evening, starting from the moment He came through the door.

cards.question: When Jesus entered Simon's house, what did Simon not give Him?
Simon greeted Jesus with a kiss when He arrived.

cards.text: But the woman, Jesus says, has not stopped kissing His feet since He arrived. Simon's sitting there like a host who forgot to put out the cookies, and Jesus is only now getting to the oil.

cards.question: Simon did not anoint Jesus' ___ with oil, but the woman anointed His ___ with perfume.

cards.text: Now Jesus brings it all home, right back to that story about the two men and the moneylender.

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon that the woman's many sins have been forgiven. What does He say about her?
Jesus says the one who has been forgiven little loves little.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks straight to the woman: "Your sins are forgiven." And the other folks at the table start talking to themselves.

cards.question: What do the people at the table begin to say to themselves about Jesus?

answers.text: Who is this who even forgives sins
Why does He let this woman stay
How does He know what Simon thinks

cards.question: Jesus has one more thing to tell the woman: "Your ___ has saved you; go in peace."

cards.text: Soon afterward, Jesus is on the move from one town and village to another, preaching the good news of the kingdom of God. After all those years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, a road trip sounds AMAZING to me.

cards.question: The Twelve are with Jesus as He travels from town to town.

cards.text: Some women are with Him too, women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities. One of them is Mary called Magdalene.

cards.question: Mary called Magdalene is the woman from whom ___ demons had gone out.

cards.text: There's Joanna, the wife of Chuza, who manages the household of Herod, ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1). Then there's Susanna, and many others.

cards.question: Joanna, Susanna and many other women are traveling along. What are these women doing?

answers.text: Ministering out of their own means
Preparing each town ahead of time
Teaching the crowds in each village

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "I heard that.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "___, I have something to tell you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke guesses that a Pharisee's house is a stiff, fussy place. That gives Simon and the Pharisees a trait the text never gives them, and it pokes at a group of people in the story instead of their human situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The Pharisees appear here for the first time, and nothing says simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply a word from inside Jesus' quoted line. The word is the host's name, which no earlier card mentions. The baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, so it can't be reasoned out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers ('Not tonight Teacher' and 'Some other time Teacher') are the same refusal. That makes 'Tell me Teacher' the only answer that's different, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A cup to drink from' isn't shown false anywhere in the passage. The text never says Simon gave Jesus a drink, so a baker could argue that Simon didn't give one either.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The comparison (a host who forgot to put out the cookies) runs into the Bible setting ('Jesus is only now getting to the oil'). The second half doesn't click without explaining.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess a word inside Jesus' quoted line, and no card sets up faith. Also, the wrong answer 'tears' doesn't fit the grammar ('Your tears has saved you'), so it's ruled out by grammar alone.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The Twelve appear here for the first time, and nothing says simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Most story cards have no humor, and the jokes that are there are mild ('Story time just became quiz time, friend', 'that little inside voice we ALL have'). They read like a pleasant dad, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
